title: Tallinn Black Nights Festival Sets Focus on Baltic Cinema for 30th Anniversary Special Edition (EXCLUSIVE)
description: To celebrate its 30th anniversary, the Tallinn Black Nights Film Festival (also known as PÖFF), the largest and only A-list festival in the Baltics,
body:
To celebrate its 30th anniversary, the Tallinn Black Nights Film Festival (also known as PÖFF), the largest and only A-list festival in the Baltics, is turning the spotlight on Baltic Cinema, with the backing from the Estonian Film Institute, National Film Centre of Latvia and Lithuanian Film Centre. 

	“Baltic cinema has always been an essential part of PÖFF,“ stated Triin Tramberg, PÖFF long-time film curator who will for the first time serve as artistic director in lieu of festival founder Tiina Lokk, now fully-focused on her CEO duties and strategic issues. 
	

	While reiterating past achievements such as the launch of the Baltic Film Competition in 2008 and Doc@PÖPP competition in 2025, Tramberg said this year’s Baltic Focus will further draw international attention to Baltic films, but also to the “remarkable talent behind them.“ 


	“The Baltic countries may be small individually, but together they form a dynamic and increasingly visible film region,“ she pointed out, referring notably to the first ever Oscar from the region for Latvia’s animation pic “Flow“ in 2025, Sundance Best Direction Award to Estonia’s “Smoke Sauna Sisterhood“ in 2023 and Locarno’s top Golden Leopard Award to Lithuania’s “Toxic“ in 2024. More recent examples of prestigious fest bows take in the Cannes Un Certain Regard entry “Ulya“ by Latvian filmmaker Viesturs Kairišs and a Cannes Special Screening for “Vesna“ by Lithuanian-born Rostislav Kirpicenko. 

	At this year’s PÖFF, the focus will be both on today’s most outstanding recent films and co-productions from the Baltics across fiction and documentary, and on past film pearls, with retrospectives including two to four landmark features from Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania. 
	

	Through the festival’s influential Industry@Tallinn & Baltic Event, attended by over 800 delegates in 2025, the Focus will further highlight upcoming Baltic film gems, the region’s top film professionals, infrastructure and tax incentives (up to 30% for Lithuania, 40% for Estonia and 50% for Latvia) that have boosted foreign filming over the past decade. Indeed examples of Baltic shores used as go-to destination for Hollywood and Euro pics abound, from “Tenet“ and “The Agency” in Estonia and “Stranger Things” and “Sisi” in Lithuania, to “The Chronology of Water” and  Venice-bound “Woman Unknown“ in Latvia. 

	Baltics Global ReachCommenting on the Baltics Focus and PÖFF at 30, Edith Sepp, CEO at the Estonian Film Institute said, “For the Estonian Film Institute, as well as for all Estonians, PÖFF turning 30 is something quite extraordinary! The festival has grown alongside the modern Estonian film industry, and in many ways, we have grown stronger together.

	“30 years ago, it would have been almost impossible to imagine Tallinn becoming a place where the international film industry shoots its films, and then every November gathers to celebrate cinema. Today, just as the Estonian film industry is not only Estonian but very international and focuses on co-productions, PÖFF together with Baltic Event is no longer simply a local festival. It is one of the platforms through which Estonia speaks to the world. And putting the spotlight on the Baltics this year is particularly important.”

	“Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania together have a stronger voice in European cinema and beyond. We all have very distinctive filmmakers, stories and cinematic cultures, and we need a platform like PÖFF that allows our films and filmmakers to shine internationally,” she said. 

	Sharing Sepp’s views, the head of the Lithuanian Film Centre Laimonas Ubavičius said, “we can take great pride in the close collaboration between the three Baltic countries and in how much our film industries have grown and strengthened. This is reflected in the increasing international recognition of Baltic cinema, the growing confidence in our producers and the emergence of a new generation of filmmakers with distinctive voices. 

	“The presentation of co-productions such as “Ulya” and “Vesna” at this year’s Cannes Film Festival is just one example of what this sustained partnership can achieve. As the festival celebrates its 30th anniversary, there is much to reflect on, and even more to look forward to,” he observed. 
	

	The 30th PÖFF will unfold both in Estonia’s capital Tallinn and second largest city Tartu Nov. 6- 22. 



	

					Triin Tramberg, Tallinn Black Nights Film Festival

schema.headline: Tallinn Black Nights Festival Sets Focus on Baltic Cinema for 30th Anniversary Special Edition (EXCLUSIVE)

title: Theo James Steps Into His Michael Corleone Era for a Darker, More Sinister ‘The Gentlemen’ Season 2: TV Review
description: It’s been two and a half years since Guy Ritchie ushered viewers into the dazzling, violent criminal underworld of his Netflix series “The Gentlemen
body:
It’s been two and a half years since Guy Ritchie ushered viewers into the dazzling, violent criminal underworld of his Netflix series “The Gentlemen.” Now, in an even darker and more volatile second season, audiences are reentering this world, with a very different Eddie (an exceptional Theo James) at the center. Engaging, devastating and thoroughly entertaining, it’s clear that with its second season, “The Gentlemen” has upped the ante and fully hit its stride.
	

	When viewers last saw Eddie, he was finding his bearings as the recently instated Duke of Halstead, and was navigating the unhinged antics of his constantly coke-out older brother Freddy (Daniel Ings), who was suffocating with bitterness after being usurped by his younger brother for their father’s title. The Duke was also learning the inner workings of an extensive cannabis empire, housed on his family’s massive estate and run by the incarcerated ​​Bobby Glass (Ray Winstone) and his whip-smart daughter, Susie (Kaya Scodelario). A former Army Captain, Eddie initially felt out of his element. Yet, as he and Susie bonded and he leaned into his military training, Eddie slowly realized being a gangster suited him as well as his tailored coats.


	As Season 2 opens, Eddie is worse for the wear. Half-dead and dragging himself on his belly through a muddy field, Eddie is far from the calm, affable aristocrat audiences first met in Season 1. But this is not where this new chapter truly begins. Dialing back three months earlier, things were looking much different for the Duke.​Firmly settled into his enterprise with the Glasses and getting Freddy sequestered away in rehab, Eddie has his sights set on expanding. Not only does he want to reclaim the land surrounding his family’s 15,000-acre estate, but he’s focused on growing the enterprise beyond the U.K., and into Italy, while gaining a stronghold in the world of legal cannabis. Yet, this will take a great deal of finesse, including pushing through a bill in parliament by buttering up Lord Hawthorne (Hugh Bonneville), who is willing to trade his vote for a night out with Susie’s brother, Jack (Harry Goodwins). As Eddie’s work wife and business partner, Susie sees the Duke’s vision, but Bobby has the final say. Bobby is open to a partnership with Italian mobster Marco Moretti (Sergio Castellitto) and his unhinged liaison Cico Maldini (Michele Morrone). However, in Bobby’s purview, decriminalizing marijuana is out of the question.​Unfortunately, Eddie and even Susie have grown increasingly weary of being under Bobby’s thumb. It’s also concerning that the older man is acting erratically and seems more focused on his spiritual awakening than on keeping his business relevant in the 21st century. Frustrated, both Susie and Eddie follow their own paths. Still, extricating oneself from Bobby’s grasp was always going to be trickier and bloodier than one would expect. While Susie is willing to comply with her father’s wishes, Eddie grows more emboldened, fueled by the power he’s learned to harness. Additionally, he begins to recognize his kindness and affability are being taken for weakness.​Exquisitely shot, “The Gentlemen” Season 2 is full of absurd characters, gunfights, hijinks (including million-dollar birds and shocking beheadings) and a couple of steamy romances. Amid the bloodbaths and whimsy, however, Eddie is evolving into someone new. Episode 4, “The Bigger Picture,” acts as a turning point in the series. Eddie, no longer able to temper his frustrations, explodes, revealing a side of himself that changes how the Glasses and viewers will see him moving forward.​With a more somber tone and higher stakes, “The Gentlemen” Season 2 is still wildly entertaining. If audiences were paying attention, there was only one way for Eddie to evolve. He was always destined to follow in the footsteps of another tyrannical, ruthless Don – Michael Corleone. But that’s the thing about becoming a crime boss: ego and power often lead to irreparable brokenness. Only time will tell how spectacular and bloody Eddie’s rise and eventual demise will be.
	

	“The Gentlemen” Season 2 is now streaming on Netflix

schema.headline: Theo James Steps Into His Michael Corleone Era for a Darker, More Sinister ‘The Gentlemen’ Season 2: TV Review

title: Andrew Garfield Hasn’t Seen ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ Yet and Insists He’s Not in ‘Avengers: Doomsday’
description: Andrew Garfield isn’t ready to reach out to Tom Holland about the massive success of “Spider-Man: Brand New Day” or “The Odyssey,” for that matter.
body:
Andrew Garfield isn’t ready to reach out to Tom Holland about the massive success of “Spider-Man: Brand New Day” or “The Odyssey,” for that matter.

	For good reason — he hasn’t seen either film.

	“I don’t want to be disingenuous,” Garfield told me Wednesday at the premiere of his historical action drama “The Uprising” at the DGA in West Hollywood. “A movie making money and people going to see it is an incredible thing, but I will reach out to him once I’ve seen [“Spider-Man”], which I’m very excited to see. And his other film, ‘The Odyssey,’ I haven’t managed to see either yet. I will send him a message when I see the work he has done.”
	

Andrew Garfield says he hasn’t congratulated Tom Holland on the success of “Spider-Man: Brand New Day” because he hasn’t seen it yet: “I don’t want to be disingenuous.” pic.twitter.com/t6XiDezh3y— Variety (@Variety) September 3, 2026


	Garfield, who played the web-slinger in two Spidey movies and reprised his role in “Spider-Man: Now Way Home” alongside Holland and fellow former “Spider-Man” star Tobey Maguire.


	But Garfield isn’t surprised that “Spider-Man: Brand New Day” has made a staggering $891 million at the domestic box office and is predicted to become the first movie to make $1 billion in North America alone.

	“Everyone has ownership over him, he’s everybody’s, and he’s decent and he’s good and he’s ordinary, and he’s extraordinary like all of us,” Garfield said. “It’s impossible not to see yourself in that character.”


	And speaking of playing “Spider-Man” again, Garfield once again insisted he won’t be appearing “Avengers: Doomsday.” “I’m not.” he said when I asked if he’s in the upcoming MCU movie.
	

	I reminded him that he has a reputation for not telling the truth because he lied about not being in “No Way Home.” “You’ll find out, I suppose, one way or another,” Garfield said, smiling.


	In Paul Greengrass’s “The Uprising,” Garfield plays a fictional character who becomes a leader during a rebellion of thousands of commoners against King Richard II in 1831.

	Director Paul Greengrass told me Garfield insisted on doing most of his own stunts for the film’s many fight scenes. “He allowed me and what my could manage,” Garfield said. “I’m not a young guy anymore. It was a lot of ice packs on the knees.”


	See more photos from “The Uprising” premiere below.



	

					Thomasin McKenzie, Woody Norman, Katherine Waterston and Andrew Garfield at “The Uprising” Los Angeles Premiere held at DGA Theater on September 02, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. (Photo by Gilbert Flores/Variety via Getty Images)
									Variety via Getty Images
	





	

					Andrew Garfield, Woody Norman and Paul Greengrass at “The Uprising” Los Angeles Premiere held at DGA Theater on September 02, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. (Photo by Gilbert Flores/Variety via Getty Images)
									Variety via Getty Images
	





	

					Jason Blum, Thomasin McKenzie, Joanna Kaye, Paul Greengrass, Andrew Garfield, Katherine Waterston and Gregory Goodman at “The Uprising” Los Angeles Premiere held at DGA Theater on September 02, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. (Photo by Gilbert Flores/Variety via Getty Images)

title: ‘Chad Powers’ Season 2 Ending: Who Knows the Truth About Russ Holliday and What Happened to Gerry?
description:
SPOILER ALERT: This story contains spoilers for “12th Quarter,” the Season 2 finale of “Chad Powers,” now streaming on Disney + and Hulu.

	It sure
body:
SPOILER ALERT: This story contains spoilers for “12th Quarter,” the Season 2 finale of “Chad Powers,” now streaming on Disney + and Hulu.

	It sure is tough being Chad Powers.

	Infamous quarterback Russ Holliday (Glen Powell) knows this well. But he’s not going to let anything stop him from continuing his double life as the socially awkward star of the South Georgia Catfish football team — especially not his teammate Gerry (Colton Ryan), who’s closer than ever to exposing Russ’ secret. 
	

	Throughout Season 2, Gerry grows increasingly suspicious of Chad, going so far as stalking the starting quarterback and those closest to him. He doesn’t know that Russ is hiding behind that prosthetic mask, but he’s pretty sure something’s amiss. Why else would Coach Ricky (Perry Mattfeld) be sneaking over to the QB’s house? And then he spots Chad’s father, “Howard Powers” (Toby Russ), wearing a wig and prosthetic nose to the homecoming banquet. 


	In the penultimate episode, “11th Quarter,” Gerry breaks into Russ and his friend Danny’s (Frankie A. Rodriguez) house and attacks Danny. The season finale opens by revealing their ransacked basement. Gerry stole the prosthetics used to disguise Russ as Chad. Danny is OK, but there’s blood running down his face. 

	Russ, disguised as Chad, meets Gerry at a movie theater, where he finds the backup QB sitting alone in an empty theater screening “Edward Scissorhands.” It’s an ominous setting, and it’s clear that Gerry, who now has hard evidence, won’t back down silently — unless Chad offers him something. 
	

	Instead of revealing what transpires between Chad and Gerry, the episode cuts to a diner where Danny meets Russ. Ricky joins them, and she’s still upset after recently discovering Russ knew that her father, Coach Hudson (Steve Zahn), wasn’t medically cleared to return to the sidelines despite telling everyone — including Ricky — that he was. Russ shrugs off the showdown with Gerry, insisting that all he wanted was money, which Russ will get, meaning that the threat has been neutralized. 

	But Danny and Ricky aren’t falling for Russ’ carefree act, and Ricky, unable to take any more of his lies, storms out. Even when he’s alone with Danny, Russ sticks to this vague story, but he does admit that he views Danny as the one true friend he’s had, and now it’s his turn to keep him safe. 

	The following day is the Catfish’s final regular season game, and they’re facing the Texas Longhorns. If the Catfish win, they move forward to the College Football Playoffs. If they lose, their dream season ends. 

	And when the game kicks off, the pressure seems to be getting to Chad, who immediately throws an interception. In fact, Chad can’t seem to do anything right on the field. By halftime, the Catfish are losing — by a lot. 



	

					Colton Ryan as Gerry in Season 2 of “Chad Powers”
									Disney
	



	As the team heads for the locker room, Ricky goes to find Danny, who reveals he found a piece of paper in Russ’ room that lists Chad’s statistics for the game — all negative plays that would tank the Catfish’s season.

	It turns out there was more to Russ’s conversation with Gerry: the former backup quarterback demanded that Chad play a “historically bad game” so Gerry would win the bets he placed against him and win $200,000. Gerry didn’t just want the money; he wanted everyone to hate Chad just as much as they hate him. Once Chad loses the game, Gerry also insists that he take responsibility for framing him by placing a 3-d printed gun in his locker in the previous episode. If he did all that, then Gerry wouldn’t come forward with the truth about Chad Powers. A devastated Russ agrees. 

	Ricky, who now understands Gerry’s scheme, finds Russ sitting alone and tells him she got the coaching job at Syracuse. She accepted and starts tomorrow, meaning this is the last game they’ll ever play together. She also reveals that she knows about Gerry’s bet, and while there’s a million things that Chad can’t do on the field, Ricky has a few tricks up her sleeve — since she’s watched all of Russ’s old game tape from his time at Oregon.
	

	When the game resumes, Ricky takes on the role as the “Chad whisperer,” drawing up trick plays that help the Catfish get into the end zone while abiding by Gerry’s terms. It’s risky, but it works, and every score makes Gerry scream with rage as he lurks in one of the stadium’s bathrooms.

	In the final moments of the game, Chad scores the game-winning touchdown, but a penalty sets them back with just two seconds left on the clock. The only way to score is by breaking Gerry’s strict rules. As Chad weighs his options, he shares a heartfelt moment with Coach Hudson, who tells the quarterback that, no matter what happens, he’s grateful for the great season they shared and is proud of him. And he knows Chad’s late mother would have been too. 

	Chad decides to run for it and scores the game-winning touchdown — for real, this time. While everyone celebrates around them, he and Ricky search for each other in the crowd and hug, excitedly, both thankful he went for the win — despite Gerry’s threats.

	Speaking of Gerry — he storms on the field, furious that Chad broke his terms and lost the $200,000. As he charges toward Russ and Ricky, he gets punched by Tricia Yeager’s (Wynn Everett) security guard. While carrying Gerry’s limp body off the field, the bodyguard tells Chad that his name has been acquired by Yeager Family Foods, then calmly points out that Chad’s facial prosthetic has slipped, referring to him as “Mr. Holliday.”

	How did he know all of that? In a last-ditch effort, Danny revealed Chad’s true identity to Tricia, who heads the Catfish boosters, and asked for her help keeping Russ’ secret safe. Tricia agreed, but coolly explained that they’d be doing things her way — beginning with having Russ and Danny move onto her ranch, so she can keep them “safe” and ensure that Russ stays as Chad “for a long time.” 

	Elsewhere on the field, Hudson tells his assistants, Coach Byrd (Quentin Plair) and Coach Dobbs (Clayne Crawford), that this will be his last season as head coach. He wants them and Ricky, whom he doesn’t know accepted the Syracuse job, to move up the ranks. 

	Now back in the locker room, Ricky and Russ share an emotional moment while she fixes his prosthetic. Mourning that this is their last game together before she leaves for New York, Ricky starts crying. As Russ consoles her, he confesses he loves her, and the two share their first kiss. 
	

	As they begin making out more passionately, Ricky starts to pull off the remaining prosthetic on Russ’ face, but they’re interrupted when Coach Hudson throws open the locker room door. Russ turns away to hide the fact that half his prosthetic mask is out of place, but it’s unclear how much Coach Hudson saw, as the episode cuts to black.

	If “Chad Powers” gets renewed for a third season, there are many loose ends to be tied up. Did Coach Hudson recognize Russ, and can his heart handle the stress of Chad’s real identity? Will Ricky go to Syracuse — especially now that she jeopardized her career by canoodling with a player? Is Gerry really gone for good? And, most importantly, will the Catfish get to — and win — the National Championship?

	Let’s say that there are still plenty of plays for Powell and co-creator and director Michael Waldron to run on their way to the end zone.

schema.headline: ‘Chad Powers’ Season 2 Ending: Who Knows the Truth About Russ Holliday and What Happened to Gerry?

title: Oscars: Romania Selects Cannes Winner ‘Fjord’ for International Feature Race
description: “Fjord,” written and directed by Cristian Mungiu, is Romania’s submission for the 2027 Oscars in the best international feature film category, havin
body:
“Fjord,” written and directed by Cristian Mungiu, is Romania’s submission for the 2027 Oscars in the best international feature film category, having been unanimously chosen by the country’s selection committee.

	The film premiered in the official competition at the Cannes Film Festival, where it won the Palme d’Or for best film, the FIPRESCI Prize, the Ecumenical Jury Prize, the Prix de la Citoyenneté and the François Chalais Prize.
	

	Sebastian Stan and Renate Reinsve star in the lead roles, with cinematography by Tudor Vladimir Panduru, editing by Mircea Olteanu, and production design by Simona Pădurețu.


	“Fjord” is a co-production involving Romania, France, Norway, Sweden, Denmark and Finland; it is produced by Mobra Films in co-production with Why Not Productions, Eye Eye Pictures, Film i Väst, Filmgate Films, Garagefilm International, Snowglobe, Aamu Film Company and France 3 Cinéma. The film was made with the support of the Romanian National Film Centre (CNC) and backed by Eurimages and the Creative Europe MEDIA Programme.

	The film was released in France on Aug. 19, and is scheduled for release in Romania this winter. Goodfellas is the film’s international sales agent, while Neon Rated is handling distribution in the U.S.

	The shortlist for the 2027 Oscar nominations will be announced by the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences on Dec. 15, with the final selection announced on Jan. 21. The 99th Academy Awards ceremony is scheduled to take place on March 14 in Los Angeles.

	“Fjord” was already eligible to be submitted for consideration in the international feature film category due to a rule change by the Academy in May. There are now two ways to submit a film for consideration for the category. In addition to a film being submitted as an official selection by a country or region, a non-English language film can now be submitted for consideration by winning best film at a major film festival. Under this rule, the following films qualify: İlker Çatak’s “Yellow Letters” (Berlin), “Fjord” (Cannes), and Visar Morina’s “Shame and Money” (Sundance, World Cinema Grand Jury Prize). The other qualifying festivals are Venice, Toronto (Platform Award) and Busan.

schema.headline: Oscars: Romania Selects Cannes Winner ‘Fjord’ for International Feature Race

title: ‘Ramayana’ Sets November Release Date
description:
Sony Pictures Entertainment is set to release “Ramayana” globally on November 6.

	The epic, starring Ranbir Kapoor, Yash and Sai Pallavi, follows e
body:
Sony Pictures Entertainment is set to release “Ramayana” globally on November 6.

	The epic, starring Ranbir Kapoor, Yash and Sai Pallavi, follows exiled prince Rama (Kapoor) and his consort Sita (Pallavi) through exile into catastrophe, as Sita’s abduction at the hands of Ravana (Yash) sets in motion an epic war between righteousness and evil.

	Nitesh Tiwari helms the two-part adaptation. Designed for audiences across cultures, it will be released in multiple languages, including English.
	

	In a trailer released earlier this Summer, audiences got a glimpse of footage showcasing high-scale visual effects, mythological weaponry, and massive battles as Rama vows to defeat Ravana across the three worlds and rescue Sita, signaling the start of the era of Rama.

	Hans Zimmer and A.R. Rahman join forces to deliver the film’s epic score. The production also features action choreography by Terry Notary and Guy Norris, and production design by Ramsey Avery and Ravi Bansal.

	The film is produced by Namit Malhotra’s Prime Focus Studios and Yash’s Monster Mind Creations. “Ramayana” Part 1 opens during the Diwali holiday frame, with Part 2 following on Diwali 2027.

	The choice of release window is no accident. Diwali – one of the most widely observed festivals in the Hindu calendar – marks the return of Rama to his kingdom of Ayodhya after 14 years of exile and his victory over Ravana. The lighting of lamps that defines the celebration is said to represent the illumination of Ayodhya on the night its beloved prince came home.

	“Ramayana” is planned as a two-part movie event based on the 5,000-year-old saga and is envisioned as an unprecedented cinematic spectacle for global audiences, with both parts filmed for Imax.
	

	DNEG – the eight-time Oscar-winning VFX house, whose credits include the “Dune” movies, “Interstellar” and “Inception” – is handling visual effects. Tiwari, whose “Dangal” remains the highest-grossing Indian film ever made, directs from a screenplay by Shridhar Raghavan.

	The film’s Indian distribution will be handled by media personality Karan Johar’s Dharma Productions.

title: ‘Anatomy of a Portrait’ Profiles Fernanda Wittgens, Italy’s First Female Museum Director and an Anti-Fascist Activist
description:
“Anatomy of a Portrait” (“Anatomia di un Ritratto”) will have its world premiere in the Venetian Nights program of Venice Days on Sept. 4. 

	Direct
body:
“Anatomy of a Portrait” (“Anatomia di un Ritratto”) will have its world premiere in the Venetian Nights program of Venice Days on Sept. 4. 

	Directed by Francesco Clerici (“Hand Gestures”) and Mattia Colombo (“Trees That Walk,” “I Wanna Sleep With You”), the documentary pieces together the story of Fernanda Wittgens, Italy’s first female museum director. Fernanda led the Pinacoteca di Brera in Milan during WWII and through its period of reconstruction. A courageous anti-fascist activist during the Mussolini regime, she was sentenced by the Fascist Special Tribunal to 20 years in prison, but was released after the war ended.
	



	

									Art historian Giovanna Ginex and actress Sara Drago on set. Courtesy of Francesco Clerici and Mattia Colombo.
	



	Having very limited historical material about Fernanda at their disposal, the directors decided to bring together actress Sara Drago and art historian Giovanna Ginex into a recording studio in order to “bring to life” Fernanda’s voice based on her letters and Giovanna’s extensive research on Fernanda’s life for nearly 40 years.


	“In a sense, ‘Anatomy of a Portrait’ is a ‘requiem for the biopic’: it is a film not about the impossibility of telling a life story “truthfully,” but about the meaning that life can hold today, and it is only natural that the archival footage and historical reconstruction – which initially seem essential – gradually dissolve into the present, transforming into a confrontation with contemporary realities and urgent issues,” Clerici and Colombo told Variety.

	The Italian-Swiss documentary is produced by Marco Malfi Chindemi’s Rossofilm with Luce Cinecittà and Lab 80 Film, in co-production with Rough Cat and RSI – Radiotelevisione Svizzera.
	



	

									Francesco Clerici and Mattia Colombo.
	



	Variety interviewed the directors Francesco Clerici and Mattia Colombo shortly before its Venice world premiere.

	How did you decide how you would tell Fernanda’s story?

	Francesco Clerici: What really remains of Fernanda Wittgens are her letters (only those she wrote, not those she received), a few photographs and a five-second clip from a video. That was our starting point: to think about how to tell her story, not by forcibly filling in the gaps left behind, but – as the film puts it – by ‘respecting’ them. A biopic is always an act of hagiographic fabrication, and it immediately struck us as a contrivance born of convention, but not the right approach.

	The turning point came when we met art historian Giovanna Ginex for a preliminary interview about Fernanda Wittgens. We realized that what really mattered was not only what remained of Fernanda, but how she continued to resonate in someone who had devoted so much of her life to studying her. Giovanna had spent almost forty years researching Fernanda and, in a way, had already created her own portrait of her.

	So we began to think that perhaps we shouldn’t try to fill the absence of images at all, but instead film what happens when someone tries to bring a person back through the traces she has left behind. We brought in Sara Drago, an actress from another generation, to give Giovanna’s imagined Fernanda Wittgens a voice, a body and a gaze. But we weren’t interested in having an actress simply impersonate Fernanda. We wanted to see whether an actress could become a space through which Fernanda might somehow reappear.

	The film became the encounter between two women — an art historian and an actress — rather than the reconstruction of a life. Wittgens’s voice passing through Giovanna, finding a new voice and body in Sara, and finally reaching us.

	How important is Brera today within the context of the art world in Italy and the world at large?

	Mattia Colombo: What makes Brera unique – quite apart from the undeniable importance of the ‘Supermasterpieces’ by Raffaello, Piero della Francesca, Caravaggio, Mantegna and so on – is that it is a museum designed for the city and its inhabitants, not just for tourists. It is designed to foster reflection, workshops, exhibitions, experiences and dialogues with the city, each time in a different way: it is a museum that engages with the local community, rather than simply being a destination for tourists.
	

	Of course, Brera has changed enormously since Fernanda’s time, but when we look at the museum today, we can still see traces of her vision. And perhaps most importantly, there are people at Brera today who still look to Fernanda as an example and who, in their own way, are trying to carry forward the work she began.

	Why do you think it’s important to tell Fernanda’s story now?

	Clerici: Amid the resurgence of fascism and the far right, and the disregard for art as a form of memory and value – and, more generally, in a world that is dramatically similar to the one in which Wittgens had to struggle to assert her authority as a woman in an almost entirely male-dominated institutional world – her story feels particularly relevant today.

	What feels equally contemporary to us is her belief in art and cultural institutions as something profoundly public and political. Fernanda risked her life not only to protect works of art during the war, but also to help politically persecuted people escape the Fascist regime. And after the war, she fought to rebuild Brera as a museum that was open and accessible to everyone. For her, preserving art, making it accessible and defending freedom were deeply connected acts.

schema.headline: ‘Anatomy of a Portrait’ Profiles Fernanda Wittgens, Italy’s First Female Museum Director and an Anti-Fascist Activist

title: Warner Music India Unveils Season 2 of Folk Music Franchise ‘Maati’ (EXCLUSIVE)
description: Warner Music India has launched season two of “Maati,” its folk music franchise, opening on Sept. 3 with the Sufi qawwali “Jalwa-e-Jaanaan” as the e
body:
Warner Music India has launched season two of “Maati,” its folk music franchise, opening on Sept. 3 with the Sufi qawwali “Jalwa-e-Jaanaan” as the eight-track season begins rolling out across eight languages.

	Anurag Saikia composed the music for the first track, which features vocals by Jyoti Nooran and lyrics by Shakeel Azmi. This qawwali is based on the Sufi concept of Wahdat al-Wujud, also known as the Unity of Being. The song examines the connection between the seeker and the creator. 
	

	Season 2 spans the Koshur/Hindi, Tamil, Bhojpuri, Punjabi, Telugu, Haryanvi, Urdu and Kannada languages. The lineup brings together contemporary and folk artists including Shubha Mudgal, Alif, Sudan, Orfo, Sublahshini, Keli Thee, Saikia, Nooran, Kalpana Patowary, Mangli, Sanjith Hegde, MC Square and Satindar Sartaj. 


	Each track in the new season is tied to a specific place tied to its tradition, with the artists, communities and regional settings built into the visual presentation of the music itself. 

	Nooran said, “‘Jalwa-e-Jaanaan’ carries a beautiful thought that the divine and the seeker are not separate, but find meaning in each other. Singing a piece with such depth was a truly soulful experience, and I hope its emotion resonates with listeners beyond language.” 

	Saikia said the track’s soundscape aimed to hold the depth of Azmi’s poetry and Nooran’s voice while retaining the soul of Sufi music. “The song explores love, devotion and the pursuit of the divine, and Maati gave us the opportunity to revisit this timeless tradition through a contemporary musical lens while staying true to its essence,” he said. 
	

	“Maati” launched in October 2024 and its debut season has reached more than 78 million digitally. Season 2 widens that footprint, extending the franchise’s musical and cultural range while keeping its focus on its traditions. 

	Jay Mehta, managing director of Warner Music India and SAARC, said, “India’s folk traditions are a living part of our culture. They carry stories, ideas and ways of seeing the world that have travelled across generations. With ‘Maati,’ our ambition is to bring these traditions to new audiences while giving the artists and communities behind them the recognition they deserve. Season 2 takes that ambition further, bringing together languages, artists and cultural landscapes, while staying true to the music at its heart.”

schema.headline: Warner Music India Unveils Season 2 of Folk Music Franchise ‘Maati’ (EXCLUSIVE)

title: Utopai Studios, DeNA Team on AI-Assisted Animation Projects in Japan (EXCLUSIVE)
description:
Utopai Studios and DeNA Co., Ltd. have unveiled an AI-assisted animation partnership in Japan. 

	The Entertainment Development Business Unit of DeN
body:
Utopai Studios and DeNA Co., Ltd. have unveiled an AI-assisted animation partnership in Japan. 

	The Entertainment Development Business Unit of DeNA will begin weaving Utopai’s storytelling AI system, PAI, into its experimental animation workflows.

	“Japan is one of the world’s most important and influential animation markets, and DeNA brings a deep understanding of both its creators and audiences,” said Cecilia Shen, CEO and co-founder of Utopai Studios. “By integrating PAI into an animation-production workflow in Japan, we are building a model that combines new production capabilities with the artistry, judgment and authorship that define great animation. This collaboration is an important step for Utopai Studios in Japan and the foundation for a relationship we believe can grow significantly over time.”
	

	PAI is already active elsewhere in the region. Huace Film & TV in China has built the system into its long-form content pipeline and is applying it to the animated series “Journey to the West: The Lost Five Hundred Years.” Utopai says the tool is also running on film and television projects in the U.S. and on international co-productions spanning Europe, North America and Asia.


	Under the Japan arrangement, a team of Utopai AI production specialists will sit alongside DeNA’s creative and production staff, contributing to early visual concepts, character and environment design, how scenes are planned and the iterative production process. DeNA’s artists keep authority over story, visual style, performances and tone, with final sign-off on every creative decision.
	

	Minabe Naoki, head of DeNA’s Entertainment Development Business Unit, said animation production demands an especially high degree of creativity, consistency and attention to detail. “Through our collaboration with Utopai Studios, we will explore how AI can help create an environment where creators can focus on their craft while making production workflows more efficient. As an initiative separate from the other animation productions currently underway at our company, we will combine the strengths of both companies and open new paths for Japan’s anime industry to continue competing globally.”

	PAI is built to hold a project’s continuity across many shots, scenes and episodes rather than generate isolated clips: once a character, background or design element is approved, its agent-first architecture can carry that asset forward into later scenes instead of rebuilding it each time, spanning everything from early visualization through final edits and asset storage. Use of production materials and creative assets in the DeNA partnership will fall under jointly negotiated rules on permissions, IP and security, with PAI initially confined to this evaluation phase.

	DeNA, founded in Tokyo in 1999 and listed on the Tokyo Stock Exchange, spans mobile games, live-streaming and sports alongside its entertainment business. Utopai Studios, which pairs original IP development with its AI production infrastructure, also operates units in the Asia-Pacific region and in Germany.

schema.headline: Utopai Studios, DeNA Team on AI-Assisted Animation Projects in Japan (EXCLUSIVE)

title: George Lucas Says Opening Lucas Museum ‘Almost Broke My Will’: ‘It’s Taken So Long to Get Here’
description: George Lucas previewed the long-in-the-works Lucas Museum of Narrative Art in Los Angeles on Wednesday, and Lucas said of the Herculean effort, “I’
body:
George Lucas previewed the long-in-the-works Lucas Museum of Narrative Art in Los Angeles on Wednesday, and Lucas said of the Herculean effort, “I’m fascinated by doing things that people say can’t be done.”

	“I’m used to doing the impossible,” said the “Star Wars” creator, who, along with his wife Mellody Hobson, has been working on the museum concept for 17 years. “Part of the problem is I’m a contrarian. I’m fascinated by doing things that people say can’t be done. This one almost broke my will.”

	In addition to a gallery packed with life-sized props from Star Wars movies, the 300,000 square foot spaceship-like museum next to the L.A. Memorial Coliseum features more than 30 galleries packed with Lucas’ collection of narrative art — from an extensive collection of Norman Rockwell paintings to works by Frida Kahlo, Diego Rivera, Maxfield Parrish and Frank Frazetta, to rooms of photography, comic book art and Western paintings and sculptures.

	Why narrative art? For Lucas, art and culture are inextricably combined.

	“It’s something that I felt very, very strongly about in terms of honoring illustrators, artists who illustrate stories that are already written, and most of the stories are myths; they’re not real, but the illustrations make them real,” Lucas said. “A picture is very powerful, and the stories are very powerful, and you combine them together, and those two elements create a society.”

	Lucas also recognized the museum staff and creators, saying “the great people that we’ve assembled to do this have been a big advantage.” The museum is designed by Ma Yansong of MAD with Stansec, with landscape architecture by Mia Lehrer.

	Check out some of the movie-themed pieces at the museum, which opens to the public Sept. 22.

title: Blueface Buys $2.2 Million California Home for Growing Family
body:
Blueface
                          New Baby, New $2.2M Home!!!
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              September 2, 2026
                            5:59 PM PDT
                                                                            
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Blueface has a new baby ... and now, a new home for his growing family ... TMZ has learned.
      
    
            Sources familiar with the sale ... the rapper recently moved into a sprawling $2.25 million property in Moorpark, California ... just in time for the arrival of his newborn son. The home spans over 5,000 square feet and features five bedrooms, five and a half bathrooms, mountain views and a four-car garage.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Blueface was chauffeured to the gated property in a Maybach Sprinter provided by Stratos. He was accompanied by Christian Crane of Agents of LA, who represented him in the purchase, along with former Death Row Records producer and real estate investor Eric "C-Style" Yokoyama.
      

            The closing gift was anything but ordinary ... Agents of LA presented Blueface with a custom gold key featuring Jesus Christ. The rapper was photographed wearing the key around his neck.
      
    
            The purchase continues Blueface's relationship with Crane, who previously worked with the rapper on his Canyon Country property.
      
    
            The big move also had a reality TV feel ... and that may not be a coincidence. Agents of LA owner Tai Savet, creator of VH1's "Love & Listings," was on the scene and teased the possibility of another real estate show.
      
    
            Savet tells TMZ ... "We might just see another real estate show inspired by this world coming to the urban market."
      
    
            Congrats on the new digs, Blue!!!

title: Disney Star Carla Jeffery Dead at 33
body:
'Zombies' Star Carla Jeffery
                          Dead at 33
                      
      
    
            Disney star Carla Jeffery -- known for her role as Bree in "Z-O-M-B-I-E-S" -- has passed away.
      
    
            Her talent agency, Alexanders Talent Management, announced the sad news on Instagram, writing ... "It is with profound sadness that we share the passing of our beloved Carla Jeffery."
      
    
            According to the agency, the actress died Tuesday. No cause of death has been disclosed at this time.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            ATM continued ... "For more than 20 years, we had the privilege of watching her grow into a beautiful, vibrant, and incredibly talented woman whose radiant smile could light up any room."
      

            They said Carla was "more than a client" ... calling her "family" in the heartbreaking announcement.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            The agency says their hearts are with Carla's loved ones during this tough time, and asks the public to honor and respect their privacy.
      
    
            The statement concludes ... "Rest beautifully, Carla. Your light will never be forgotten."
      
    
            She was 33.
      
    
            RIP

title: Tim Curry's Cause of Death Revealed
description:
'Rocky Horror' Star Tim Curry
                          Cause of Death Revealed
body:
'Rocky Horror' Star Tim Curry
                          Cause of Death Revealed
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              
                September 2, 2026
                
                            12:24 PM PDT
                                                                      |
                                                                Updated 
                                  September 2, 2026
                                2:34 PM PDT
                                    
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Tim Curry died from coronary artery disease, TMZ has confirmed.
      
    
            The Los Angeles County Department of Public Health made the determination -- first reported on by People -- that coronary artery disease was Tim's main cause of death. Kidney cancer and his history of strokes were listed as underlying causes.
      
    
            We broke the story ... Tim died at his Los Angeles-area home on Tuesday. Law enforcement sources told us no foul play was suspected.
      

            He dealt with health issues over the years ... most notably suffering a stroke back in 2012, which significantly decreased his mobility. He used a wheelchair through the rest of his life.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Tim -- best known for his roles in musical movies like "The Rocky Horror Picture Show" and "Annie" -- looked to be doing all right when a caregiver helped him into a North Hollywood pub in April, a few days after his 80th birthday.
      
    
            He was even working in the months before his death -- shooting all the scenes for the upcoming horror flick "STREAM 2: Sudden Death."
      
    
            Tim was 80 years old.
      
    
            RIP
